title: Six men from Yathrib
hookLine: at the pilgrimage six men from Yathrib listen and believe
last: HE WEIGHED THE SPEAKER, NOT THE DISTANCE.

cards: Tents and travelers fill the valleys around Mecca, tribes come from far away, and Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, made a habit of these crowds: camp to camp, introducing himself, asking who would hear him out.
Mostly they turned away. After Ta'if, after the mocking, he keeps going. Then one evening, near a place called Aqaba, he meets a small group from a town to the north.
Ibn Ishaq counts them: six men from Yathrib. He asks them a simple question. Will you sit with me, and let me speak to you?

teach.b: They sit. He tells them about God and recites the Qur'an. And something, Ibn Ishaq says, had already prepared them.
In Yathrib they lived beside Jewish neighbors, people of scripture, who had spoken of a prophet who would come.
So the six look at each other: this may be the prophet they told us about. Let's not be the last to answer him. And they believe.
They tell him about home, too.

teach.h: A TOWN WORN DOWN BY FEUDS.
teach.b: Yathrib was worn down by feuding between its own clans: we have left our people, and no people are so divided by enmity as they are. Perhaps God will unite them through you.
We'll go home and call them to this, and if God gathers them around you, no man will be stronger than you. Then they go home and talk.
Before long, Ibn Ishaq says, there was hardly a house in Yathrib where the Prophet wasn't spoken of. Look at the shape of it. Years of closed doors in Mecca.
A walk to Ta'if that ended in stones. Then six strangers, from a town he has never lived in, who simply listen. Nobody argues them into it.
They sit, they hear, they take it home.
A new part of the story begins: toward Yathrib, the town that will one day be called Medina, the city.

how: Muslims retell the meeting with the six men of Yathrib as the start of the road to Medina, the turning point after the hardest years in Mecca.

games.q: you're one of six travelers at the pilgrimage. a man from Mecca, rejected by many, asks if you'll sit and let him speak. what do you do?
o: keep walking; you've heard about him.
games.why: they sat and listened, and said: this may be the prophet our neighbors spoke of. let's not be the last to answer him.

practice: Think of a stranger you're likely to meet soon: someone at a counter, a new person at work, a neighbor you've only nodded to.
Picture letting them finish, not planning your reply, not checking the time, just hearing what they have to say. If you pray, you can ask God for an open ear.

wordCard.voice: Yathrib. The town, later called Medina, whose six strangers sat, listened to the Prophet at the pilgrimage, believed, and carried the news home. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Yathrib, the town's name before it was called Medina.

carryVoice: Your line: six listened. Big turns can start that small. Day seven hundred fifty-eight, done.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (he offers himself to the tribes at the fairs; six men of Yathrib meet him at Aqaba, recall what their Jewish neighbors said of a coming prophet, believe, and hope he will unite their people)
